Nothing in the statement needs it. `modularFunctionFieldC K N` (IntermediateField.adjoin K {jqModC K, jqNModC K N}) only needs `[Field K]` and `[NeZero N]`. So do `jGeomGen K N := ⟨jqModC K, jqModC_mem K N⟩` (Def_ModularCurve_CharLSpecialFibreLevelNDictionary.lean, section variables `(K) [Field K] (N) [NeZero N]`) and `IsModPFormFn K m G` (`[Field K]` only). The proof doesn't use it either. It applies `isIntegral_adjoin_of_coe`, proved in this file in a section with only `[Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]`. It then rewrites with the generic IntermediateField coercion lemmas `coe_mul`, `coe_pow`, `AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub`, and with `coe_jGeomGen`, which needs only `[Field K]` and `[NeZero N]` and is proved by `rfl`. It finishes with `hG.1`. So `omit [IsAlgClosed K] in` leaves the same proof working.

Lean makes this an argument automatically, because it is instance-implicit and its type only mentions `K`. No definition in the statement (`modularFunctionFieldC`, `jGeomGen`, `IsModPFormFn`, `Algebra.adjoin`, `IsIntegral`) requires decidable equality. The proof (`isIntegral_adjoin_of_coe`, the coercion rewrites, `coe_jGeomGen`, `hG.1`) never uses it. If elaboration did pick it up somewhere, `DecidableEq K` is a subsingleton, so the statement re-elaborated without it is still provable. Removing it with `omit [DecidableEq K] in` keeps the theorem true with the same proof. It can be removed on its own or together with `[IsAlgClosed K]`.
